PILOT: evaluates the built-in CEL posture rules (rollout safety and image-tag pinning) over Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets. The same claims `audit workloads` and `audit hardening` make in Go, authored as data; output for the shared kinds is byte-identical by test. Scope with --namespace or -A; scanned counts workloads examined.

MCP tool: `k8s_audit_rules` (MCP profile: `audit`)

## Usage

```sh
lookout audit rules [flags]
```

## Common flags (every `lookout` command)

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | string | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | bool | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | string | — | target one workload as \<Kind>/\<namespace>/\<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | duration | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | string | `logfmt` | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | duration | `10s` | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | string | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--context` | string | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=\<name> in the summary line |
| `--exemptions` | string | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=\<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing. See the [finding-kind glossary](/reference/finding-kinds/) for the whole vocabulary.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.liveness_preempts_readiness` | warning, info | liveness and readiness probe the same handler and liveness gives up no later than readiness: the kubelet restarts the container before readiness can take it out of the Service, so the readiness probe is decoration; info when the two deadlines tie, warning when liveness is strictly earlier |
| `audit.rollout_drops_traffic` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica workload (or a Service-backed DaemonSet) whose serving container has no preStop hook: SIGTERM races endpoint removal on every rollout, drain and scale-down, and in-flight requests get connection resets |
| `audit.recreate_strategy` | warning | a Service-backed, multi-replica Deployment whose strategy permits zero surviving pods — Recreate, or rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable at or above the replica count — so every rollout is an outage the Deployment never reports |
| `audit.image_floating_tag` | warning | a container image reference names no particular bytes — a tag that by convention moves (latest, main, master, dev, nightly, stable, edge) or no tag at all, with no digest: the next pull may run different code with no deploy and no record |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `containers` | containers whose liveness probe fires no later than their readiness probe on the same handler |
| `container_names` | their names, capped at 8 with a +N more tail |
| `total_containers` | containers in the pod template, so `containers` reads as a fraction |
| `services` | Services routing to the workload whose ports are not all scrape endpoints |
| `service_names` | their names, capped at 8 with a +N more tail |
| `termination_grace` | the pod template's terminationGracePeriodSeconds (the API default of 30s when unset) |
| `replicas` | the Deployment's spec.replicas |
| `strategy` | the strategy setting that permits zero surviving pods |
| `rules` | summary note: rules evaluated per workload |
| `workloads` | summary note: workloads examined, broken down as deployments/statefulsets/daemonsets |
| `resource` | read.unavailable: the resource that could not be read, as resource[.group] |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```sh
lookout audit rules -A
lookout audit rules --namespace=prod
```
